sections.title: Scorecard and Calculation Audit
sections.text:
Canonical factors: GOV5, MOAT5, REV8, DUR6, CAP NS, CASH3, BAL NS, EXEC6, EARN6; IAS factors R NS, D3, P4, L NS. Each factor has two material facts, contrary evidence, source references and a single reused integer or null. BQS known weighted contribution 4.34 at 80% coverage has missing-data bounds 4.54–6.34. GQS known contribution 5.60 at 85% coverage has raw bounds 5.75–7.10. Persistent weak operating cash realization triggers the explicit GQS cap 5; the capped bounds 5–5 do not turn the missing CAP point into a ranked score.

IAS uses final BQS once at 25%, then R35%, D20%, P10%, L10%. Directly scoreable contribution 1.00 covers 30%; unconstrained missing-input bounds 1.70–8.00. Propagating the narrower BQS bounds gives 2.585–7.085. These are exact Decimal mathematical ranges, not probabilities or confidence intervals. Missing factors are never assigned 5 or zero, weights are not renormalized and no hidden overall score is created. G2 independently prevents a favorable IAS conclusion. GOV is not≤3 and G3 is not an evidenced failure, so neither numerical failure override applies. A one-point MOAT move changes BQS bounds 0.20; a one-point EXEC move 0.08. These sensitivities cannot cure missing capital/funding evidence. [Factor audit and exact contribution tables below]

sections.title: Business Overview
sections.text:
The group sells stainless-steel single-wall and vacuum/double-wall bottles, tumblers, feeding bottles and gym shakers. It earns manufacturing value through forming, finishing, vacuum processing, printing and packing, and commercial value through product design, sourcing, branding and distribution. Dewdrop Bottles operates the manufacturing facilities; Speedex Online supports online distribution. Two leased units divide core production from polishing/printing/packing/storage. Lease rentals remain operating costs under the actual Accounting Standards basis; no separate operational-property value is added to enterprise value.

FY24 was a 100% trading business in the issuer perimeter. Following acquisition of formerly promoter-linked entities, FY26 manufactured goods contributed 88.85% and traded products 11.15%. This is not a pure brand or pure contract manufacturer: OEM contributed 54.87% ofrevenue, own brand 41.81%, with the remainder principally scrap. Brand share fell from 45.51% although absolute branded sales increased. Online share was 9.91%; most sales still pass through offline distributors, institutional/OEM buyers and channel relationships. The network comprises 101 distributors across 17 states and 2 union territories, not a verified count of exclusive consumer touchpoints.

Customers purchase utility, design, quality and price; OEM customers can award volume without granting a durable brand premium. Nonexclusive distribution and customer concentration limit bargaining power. Revenue recognition does not equal cash collection: inventory must be funded, OEM/distributor credit collected, and material purchases paid. Steel input cost, production yield, mix, returns/warranty obligations, freight and retailer economics determine the spread. Segment-level margin and brand-versus-OEM ROIC are ND, so they are not filled from consolidated profitability. [E02,E04–E08]

sections.title: Moat / Industry Position
sections.text:
The plausible advantage is an integrated manufacturing/process base combined with established channel relationships and a recognizable niche brand. Mechanism: consistent steel quality, finish and delivery can win repeat OEM/distributor orders and reduce outsourced production friction. Evidence: manufacturing represents 88.85%, production increased 21.37%, and the group has 101 distributors. Durability remains unproven: contracts are nonexclusive, top 10 customers rose to 48.70% ofsales, own-brand share declined, and no independently verified market share or sustained pricing premium is supplied. Failure modes include customer dual sourcing, aggressive national-brand pricing, inventory markdowns and larger rivals localizing production.

Three economically relevant comparisons prevent equating small scale with an empty competitive field. Borosil's 6 February 2026 call described BIS-related constraints on Hydra and a planned ₹65 crore three-line domestic double-wall investment, approximately 4 million units annually. That is evidence of a competitor response and planned capacity, not proof those lines subsequently commissioned. Cello's FY25 annual report records ₹2136.39 crore consolidated revenue and 4000+distributors/150000+retailers; its diversified houseware range and much larger reach make its group valuation an imperfect bottle multiple. Hamilton/Milton's official Steel Halo product provides qualitative evidence of an established competing stainless-steel offering; no dynamic product price is used.

MOAT5 therefore recognizes useful but contestable operations. Certifications and reputed buyers demonstrate qualification, not a patent-like barrier. Supplier concentration is also high:87.38% fromtop 10 and 23.56% fromthe largest. Purchasing leverage or assured supply may help, but neither proves exclusive low-cost access. [E03–E06,E19]

sections.title: Revenue Growth & Scale
sections.text:
Revenue history is ₹42.6151/64.7281/61.3233/93.5081/122.6538 crore for FY22–FY26, with scope breaks clearly marked. FY22–26 mixed-scope four-year CAGR30.25%, FY23–26 three-year 23.75% and FY24–26 two-year 41.43% are descriptive only. Five-year CAGR requires six annual observations and is ND; a three/five-year organic CAGR and latest comparable interim/TTM are also ND. Annual rupee additions were ₹22.1130,−3.4048,+32.1848,+29.1457 crore. The FY24 decline should not disappear behind the later consolidation jump.

Dewdrop's legal SPA is 27 January 2025 and Speedex Online's 4 February 2025. The prospectus explicitly asserts in-substance control effective 1 April 2024 and full FY25 line-by-line consolidation, despite later legal transfer. That declared policy makes FY25→FY26 the best available constant-perimeter comparison, while FY24→FY25 is not organic. A conflicting isolated 2026 acquisition-history sentence is not silently used to splice periods.

The chosen REV basis, declared before scoring, is the single comparable full-year interval FY25→FY26:31.17% growth, ₹29.1457 crore addition. Actual production rose 21.37%, supporting volume expansion, with mix/realization and inventory timing also important. Production is not sold volume, so the residual is not labeled pure price inflation. This starts at 9 under the≥30% schedule and is capped at 8 for only two relevant audited observations and Medium confidence, with no extra trajectory adjustment. This exception acknowledges real scaling without claiming multi-year durability. [E02,E03]

sections.title: Growth Quality & Reinvestment Runway
sections.text:
The bottom-up path begins with 4.2586 million FY26 units produced and 6.282 million exit capacity. The issuer's 88.41% utilization uses time-weighted capacity because 1.758 million units were added in February; against full year-end capacity output is 67.79%. These are different valid denominators, not evidence of fabrication. The detailed engineer-backed bridge supersedes stale generic wording still referring to 4.524 million capacity. Proposed addition 2.766 million units would lift capacity to 9.048 million and requires ₹21.4158 crore of IPO allocations.

The forecast does not make that proposed capacity operational in March 2026. It assumes availability from 1 April 2027 after FY27 deployment, and tests a one-year delay plus 25% cost overrun. Before commissioning, manufactured revenue is constrained by existing capacity, utilization and an explicitly labeled realization proxy. Thereafter growth requiring more capacity incurs upfront cash capex at the proposed project's unit cost, inflated 5% annually; no unlimited growth on free plant. Manufactured/traded revenue mix is held at 88.85% manufactured share for modeling, not claimed to be management guidance. Maintenance capex is a 1.5–2% revenue assumption, not depreciation mechanically relabeled.

The opportunity is distribution expansion, premium/novelty products, OEM customers and domestic substitution, but accessible demand must be won against established brands. Book incremental ROIC33.19% is a useful diagnostic, not a mature plant return. The 2%-revenue cash-reserve sensitivity is explicit. GQS remains NS because CAP is missing, with cap 5 from recurring weak cash realization. A large market or announced machines do not establish intrinsic-value-per-share compounding. [E03–E09,E15,E19]

sections.title: Management, Governance & Execution
sections.text:
Promoters retain 63.93% after the IPO, so minority outcomes depend on related-party discipline and cash deployment. FY26 director remuneration ₹2.0523 crore equals 13.38% of PAT; it is material, but no abuse is inferred merely from the amount. Related-party debt, purchases and formerly related manufacturing/online businesses require arm's-length scrutiny. Current pledge/encumbrance confirmation is ND; an aggregator's zero is not treated as primary proof. The OFS benefits selling holders, while only the fresh issue funds the group.

The prospectus reports private-placement procedural lapses, including receipt/use processes and separate-account requirements, with voluntary adjudication submitted 2 January 2026. It attributes them to inadvertence; outcome remained pending. Other delayed filings had late fees paid and no related show-cause notice disclosed. Signing deficiencies were corrected 23 March 2026. Acquisitions initially used book values without contemporaneous independent valuation, but reports were subsequently obtained. Both the original concern and later counterevidence matter; neither is concealed and no adjudged fraud or diversion is asserted.

Promise versus delivery: the February 2026 capacity addition is reflected in engineer-certified capacity and higher output; the FY27 IPO-funded expansion is planned, not confirmed operational. The 25 September ₹19.8 crore subsidiary subscription is reported by an announcement reproduction, not authenticated underlying utilization. It is internal equity financing until the subsidiary spends externally and must not be deducted again on top of project capex. Brand mix has not yet delivered an expanding share:41.81% versus 45.51%, despite growth in absolute branded sales.

Full statutory review changes the reliability assessment. FY24 Q3 inventory reported to the bank was ₹13.1017 crore against books ₹9.5080 crore, a ₹3.59375 crore difference. FY25 Q4 bank debtors were ₹11.2251 crore against books ₹13.7423 crore,₹2.51723 crore LOWER, not evidence of inflated borrowing claims. Management cites provisional unaudited returns and later AS adjustments, reclassifications and setoffs. CARO explicitly references variances. Unmodified main opinions, FY24 clean audit-trail wording and FY25 issuer-standalone adequate/effective IFC are preserved as counterevidence. FY25 Rule 11 pages have no located audit-trail paragraph: this is ND, not a disabled-system claim. The retrieved FY25 original is issuer-standalone, not the full consolidated package. Full FY25 consolidated and FY26 statutory audit annexures and a quantified current reconciliation remain unlocated. G2 Hold is therefore a reliability limitation, not a misconduct verdict. [E10–E16]

sections.title: Financial Forensics
sections.text:
The historical tables below keep original standalone FY22–23, restated special-purpose standalone FY24 and restated consolidated FY25–26 distinct. Operating EBITDA is PBT+finance cost−other income+D&A; operating EBIT excludes other income, and normalized PAT applies 25% tax to PBT excluding other income. Gross profit is ND rather than an aggregator operating-profit substitute. All subsidiaries are wholly owned, so no NCI deduction is invented. Operating rents remain within margins under AS, with no separate property value.

FY26 operating EBITDA₹22.5948 crore versus ₹10.6303 crore demonstrates operating leverage; otherincome ₹0.0882 crore is small. Reported PAT₹15.3419 crore versus normalized ₹14.3282 crore reflects a lower reported tax burden. The fresh issue expands shares 26.72% and dilutes an unchanged holder 21.09%; these percentages are not interchangeable. Current-share-equivalent FY26 EPS₹9.3862 is lower than statutory weighted-average ₹11.89. Bonus shares alone are not economic dilution.

Comparable FY25–26 CFO₹5.7102 crore/PAT₹20.9074 crore=0.2731 x and FCF₹−7.5777 crore. The mixed-scope FY24–26 ratio 0.3566 x is only context. Cash interest ₹1.9209/1.4005 crore is classified in financing; subtracting it gives a separate after-interest conversion diagnostic 0.1143 x, not a replacement for reported CFO. Operating cash weakness is driven by working capital/tax, not by investing capex. Inventory increased ₹20.3593→36.1749 crore, receivables ₹12.5356→19.3496 crore, partly financed by payables ₹11.0696→20.3866 crore. ONWC rose ₹15.8355 crore. Most debtor ageing is under 6 months; over 1 year totals ₹0.2484 crore, with no doubtful provision. Due-date data are unavailable, so invoice-age/total-revenue days are proxies. Issuer closing inventory days 150 versus 98 versus 62 are not mixed with average-balance COGS days. FY23 original CFO includes ₹1.179327 crore financing inflow; removing it gives an analytical−₹0.764762 crore, not a corrected audit.

Book operating IC₹30.1331→55.5192 crore reconciles to equity+debt less cash/non-operating assets plus tax/gratuity funding adjustments within ₹1–2 thousand rounding. NOPAT increased ₹8.424975 crore on ₹25.3861 crore added IC, yielding 33.19% one-year incremental proxy and 36.19% average ROIC. Adding 2% revenue cash reserves gives incremental ROIC32.44% and average ROIC34.45%, for consistency with forecast reserves. The F25 fixed-asset note reconciles FY26 net assets: opening ₹6.1278 crore plus additions ₹11.1840 less disposal book value ₹0.2155 and depreciation ₹1.9303 equals ₹15.1660. Opening tangible assets differ ₹0.0130 crore from prior closing; cash capex is ₹0.0131 crore below accounting additions. Similar amounts do not establish the cause. No three/five-year stable manufacturing attribution, mature cohort profit bridge or project IRR is available; CAP stays NS.

Restatement is not suppressed: FY25 consolidated PAT₹6.6655 crore became ₹5.5655 crore, including ₹0.9831 crore unrealized intercompany inventory correction. FY26 balance-sheet networth ₹28.8624 crore conflicts with ₹28.6624 crore reconciliation, a ₹0.20 crore unresolved difference; smaller profit-adjustment inconsistencies also remain. These are not automatic cash writeoffs. The F32 related-party flow table also prints 28,000.00 in a column labeled ₹lakhs for a director loan, inconsistent with far smaller reported closing balances; F31/F33 also differ by ₹34.73 lakh, potentially because of holding/group scope. This unresolved unit/perimeter ambiguity is not treated as an actual ₹280 crore transaction or new financing. [E20] The older ₹0.6847 crore company tax contingency disappears from FY26 totals without located settlement detail; promoter personal disputes are not group obligations. [E07–E16]

sections.title: Valuation & Market Expectations
sections.text:
At ₹245.40 and 16,345,140 shares, market capitalization is ₹401.1097 crore and latest-PAT P/E26.14 x. Combining that equity price with March debt/unrestricted cash gives historical EV₹427.4088 crore and 18.92 x operating EBITDA, not current EV after IPO. Historical P/B13.90 x becomes 4.78 x on a purely pro-forma addition of net IPO proceeds, ignoring subsequent earnings, actual fees and deployment. Current EV/PB remain ND rather than mixing fresh equity with stale debt as fact.

The funding bridge removes ₹0.10 crore restricted FD, recognizes only ₹64.10304 crore fresh gross proceeds, deducts remaining fees ₹8.7033 crore after ₹0.2673 crore already prepaid, and excludes ₹16.02576 crore OFS. It conditionally repays ₹24.1043 crore bank debt and earmarks the full ₹21.4158 crore capex once. Net March tax liability ₹0.4693 crore is settled after disclosed credits, with a separate no-credit-availability stress; all ₹0.4291 crore March gratuity is reserved. Residual ₹3.9008 crore related debt bears 9% and is repaid in FY29. No dividend, optional equity, fresh bank rollover, property surplus or subsidiary transfer is silently added as cash.

Timing matters. March unrestricted cash ₹0.3642 crore is below the analyst 2% operating reserve by ₹2.088876 crore; that is not proof of actual default. Strict no-assumed-headroom paths have null return/entry points. A separate conditional branch assumes the disclosed ₹25.35 crore nominal limits are genuinely drawable, stages known March/August debt, caps extra bridge borrowing at available headroom, charges interest and repays it once. IPO cash first enters 17 September, never retroactively funds April. Current availability is unverified, so all ordinary returns/entry prices remainnull regardless of conditional model success.

Bear/base/bull use explicit growth paths, EBITDA11%/17%/20%, ONWC40%/32%/30%, exit EV/EBITDA8 x/12 x/16 x and capacity-linked reinvestment. The nominal-facility branches, if all conditions hold, have five-year returns shown in the scenario table; base is below 15%. Required operating cash remains in the business at exit. Full FY32 growth capex is paid upfront, while only cash earned through 20 October 2031 is counted. All annual rows, preentry checkpoints,18 two-way sensitivity runs and the funded reverse crossing are embedded. Margin,WC, tax-credit, claims, commissioning and overrun stresses distinguish a funded path from a rescue. Any breached non-rescue path has null returns; rescue is a rerun with explicit gross/fees/net/newshares and changed borrowing interest, not money added only at the terminal date.

DCF tests WACC12/15/18% and terminal growth 3/4/5%, with 18% terminal incremental ROIC and cash-reserve reinvestment. Terminal value is a large share, disclosed per cell. At 15% WACC/4% terminal growth, DCF is ₹100.85 per share versus the base scenario 15%-hurdle entry ₹191.82. The large spread comes from 18% perpetual incremental ROIC and reinvestment versus a 12 x EBITDA exit multiple, not rounding. These methods are not averaged into a target. DCF is a conservative cross-check, not an executable price target. Conditional 12/15/18% entry calculations cannot resolve G2 or establish current funding. [E15–E18]

sections.title: Bear Case & Permanent-Loss Path
sections.text:
The strongest bear case is not that stainless-steel bottles have no demand. It is that a newly integrated, credit-intensive supplier grows accounting earnings while OEM competition and inventory consume the economic profit. If customer concentration rises, OEM prices compress, receivables collect later and new capacity arrives into heavier domestic competition, margins and cash deteriorate together. Inventory markdowns or supplier-credit withdrawal can add pressure precisely when lenders reassess drawing power.

The explicit bear assumes initial sales decline,11% EBITDA,40% ONWC and 8 xexit. It breaches the pre-IPO analyst cash reserve by ₹0.009551 crore, so its non-rescue return is NS, not a rounded-away feasible point. The algebraic loss diagnostic and separately funded rescue path imply about 61% five-year capital loss. This small modeled reserve gap is not evidence of actual default. The linked stress combines a 4 percentage-point margin reduction,10 percentage-point ONWC increase and ₹5 crore additional claim; the fundedness test fails before assigning a return. A separate discounted-equity counterfactual demonstrates dilution, not available rescue. WC+8 percentage points alone also matters at pre IPO checkpoints, even if annual end cash would look positive.

Counterevidence is substantial: production and operating earnings grew, main audits are unmodified, IFC conclusions are not adverse, most receivables are recent, and a large fresh IPO can materially deleverage. These positives prevent an evidenced-default conclusion. The thesis-break variables are verified collection/conversion, reconciliation credibility, available funding and demand-backed plant use, not one isolated quarter or a price decline. [E03,E07–E11,E16,E17]

sections.title: 5× / 10× Feasibility
sections.text: Fivefold and tenfold equity gains in five years require 37.97% and 58.49% annualized returns respectively. At an illustrative 20 xterminal P/E and 12% PATmargin with today's shares, fivefold equity value requires roughly ₹835.65 crore sales, tenfold ₹1671.29 crore. Those are approximately 6.8 x and 13.6 x FY26 revenue before further dilution, not justified by simply installing the proposed 2.766 million units. They would need additional capacity, channels, working capital, strong margins and attractive incremental returns far beyond the demonstrated two-year manufacturing record. Bull-case upside is not proof of a 5×path, and no probability is assigned. Multibagger status: speculative/unsupported, not the investment case. [E03,E06,E09,E17]

sections.title: Monitoring Plan
sections.text:
Monitor eight concrete areas. (1) Obtain full FY26 statutory/CARO/IFC/Rule 11 material and an itemized bank-return reconciliation, explicitly separating debtor amounts below books from inventory amounts above books. (2) Reconcile the ₹0.20 crore networth difference and profit-restatement arithmetic without inventing an impairment. (3) Track actual IPO debt repayment, remaining earmarked cash, capex payments and available facilities against ₹24.1043/21.4158 crore allocations. (4) Verify commissioning, installed capacity and saleable output against 6.282 million existing/9.048 million proposed, with a dated customer-supported ramp.

(5) Follow cumulative comparable CFO/PAT from 0.273 x, ONWC/revenue from 31.93% and inventory days from issuer 150; sustained conversion below 0.6 x or fresh ageing deterioration is a warning, not an automatic fraud test. (6) Track own-brand share 41.81%, OEM54.87%, online 9.91% and top 10 customer 48.70%; rising concentration with margin erosion challenges the moat. (7) Require mature expansion/cohort or stable multi-year incremental-profit/capital evidence before scoring CAP. (8) Confirm adjudication/valuation outcomes, related debt repayment terms, current pledge status and complete BSE execution history. A lower quote alone changes valuation, not these business evidence requirements.

Analyst monitoring rules, not forecasts or allegations:
- At the next filed interim or full-year cash-flow release, recompute trailing cash conversion and ONWC. CFO/PAT below 0.5 x and ONWC above 40% of sales across two consecutive comparable releases, without a dated funded unwind, breaks the cash-compounding thesis; one seasonal quarter alone does not.
- At the next IPO-utilization/cash disclosure, reconcile proceeds, eligible capex, debt repayment, earmarks and available limits. An unexplained material funding deficit keeps G3 closed; actual unpaid debt would trigger a new survival assessment, not be inferred now.
- At the next audited FY27 package, require an itemized resolution of bank/book differences, networth and RPT scope/units. Repeated unexplained material differences keep G2 closed even if the main opinion remains clean; a signed reconciliation can improve confidence without erasing history.
- The model assumes proposed capacity available from 1 April 2027. Review commissioning and saleable production with the first FY28 interim release. A full-year delay invokes the disclosed delay case; continued delay into FY29 or unsupported utilization while capex is paid breaks the modeled expansion timetable.
- At each comparable release, check top 10 customer share 48.70%, OEM share 54.87% and operating EBITDA margin 18.42%. Customer concentration above 60% together with margins below the 11% bear level for two comparable releases would break the claimed diversified-growth economics. A changed mix alone is not failure.
 [E04–E18]

sections.title: Final Classification & Conditional Action
sections.text:
Hold — unresolved. Maharaja & Speedex has credible recent manufacturing growth and useful expansion options, but does not satisfy the full compounder test: durable advantage, attributable excess incremental returns, dependable operating cash and independently supported funding have not all been established. BQS/GQS/IAS are NS, not failed zeros, and all three ranking-eligibility flags arefalse. G1 is Conditional rather than Fail, and G3 is an evidence hold rather than an allegation of insolvency.

This is a research/watchlist category, not a buy/sell instruction or portfolio allocation. Ordinary five-year return and entry-price recommendations are withheld. Conditional scenario prices are mathematical outputs under stated facility/deployment assumptions and cannot override G2. The most valuable next evidence is a current published consolidated sources/uses bridge, full audit annexures with resolved material differences, and a mature cash-generative plant ramp. Price becomes actionable only after those constraints and actual tradability are addressed. [E09–E18]

sections.title: Sources, Assumptions & Open Questions
sections.text:
Primary source priority is the 16 September 2026 final prospectus and original FY23/FY24/FY25 statutory packages, read in full with OCR plus visual checks of material audit pages. The FY26 restated statements are primary, but their summary of unmodified underlying audits is not a replacement for missing full FY26 annexures. Official security master verifies the exact ISIN/share count/lot; price history and exchange-notice reproductions remain secondary. All cited original URLs, byte hashes, periods and locators are in the source register; raw PDFs, HTML, OCR and page images are excluded from portable analytical backups.

Assumptions are explicitly analyst estimates:25% tax,2% revenue operating cash floor, conditional nominal facility availability, staged pre IPO debt movements, FY28 operational availability of proposed capacity, maintenance 1.5–2% revenue, realization 0–3%,5% capital-cost inflation, and terminal multiples/DCF rates. These are not management promises. Historical book ROIC excludes required cash in its core definition but carries an explicit reserve-inclusive sensitivity; it is not compared unqualified with a cash-inclusive forward model.

Open questions: full FY26 audit annexures; current bank/book reconciliations and networth adjustments; current cash/drawing power and actual IPO utilization; old company tax-contingency resolution; current pledge/fully diluted claims after IPO; maturity of related finance; brand/OEM margins and sold-unit realizations; mature project/cohort returns; and complete trading-depth/restriction evidence. Offline reproduction proves arithmetic and artifact consistency, not fresh authentication of external source truth. [All source and evidence entries]
